appraisal_events.evidence: un vieil ami des Verdurin, Saniette, à qui sa timidité, sa simplicité et son bon coeur avaient fait perdre partout la considération que lui avaient value sa science d'archiviste, sa grosse fortune, et la famille distinguée dont il sortait.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator reports that Saniette's genuine virtues (shyness, simplicity, good-heartedness) have cost him the social consideration his real credentials (scholarship, wealth, family) would otherwise command, marking his diminished standing in society generally.

appraisal_events.evidence: excita chez Saniette une sympathie ardente que d'ailleurs les Verdurin ne révélèrent jamais à Swann, car Saniette les agaçait un peu, et ils ne tenaient pas à lui faire des amis.
appraisal_events.explanation: Though Swann's unusual request to meet him stirs strong warmth in Saniette, the Verdurins deliberately withhold this from Swann because Saniette mildly irritates them and they do not want him to gain friends, actively limiting his access to a valued connection.

status_effects.explanation: Saniette's personal qualities have generally cost him the social consideration his credentials would otherwise merit, marking a standing diminishment.
The Verdurins deliberately keep Saniette's warm response from Swann so as not to let him form a friendship, actively gatekeeping him from a valued social connection despite his own goodwill.

ambiguities: S2's source is jointly 'les Verdurin' (both M. Verdurin and Mme Verdurin); it is attributed here to Mme Verdurin as the dominant conversational figure in the scene, though the text presents the exclusionary motive as shared by the couple.

The Verdurins' minor irritation with Saniette and the narrator's sympathetic framing of his 'faults' as virtues could support an ironized reading of society's judgment in S1; a more conservative neutral_report stance was chosen since no explicit ironic marker targets the judgment itself.
